_comment: Every ${...} placeholder in a shipped MCP manifest that is NOT one of the three
must be listed here with a reason, or verify-pack.mjs FAILS.
Why this is an allowlist and not a denylist: the vendor doc
manifest may also carry '${ENV_VAR} from the environment' -- so these spellings
are not illegal. They are DANGEROUS, which is different: when the named variable
is UNSET, the host substitutes nothing and the child process receives the literal
eight-or-more character string '${FOO}' as the value. microsoft-365 shipped five
of these and the server crashed on startup -- measured and reproduced 2026-09-13.
A denylist of known-bad spellings would have caught ${PLUGIN_ROOT} and missed
every one of those. So: unknown placeholder = FAIL until someone writes down why.

allowed.reason: MEASURED tolerant: the WordPress/Elementor connector validates each of these and falls back to its stored profile config when the value is absent or malformed, so a literal '${OMATIC_WP_URL}' is discarded rather than executed. Left in place deliberately rather than deleted, because a SET variable is the documented way an operator overrides the profile without editing the manifest.
allowed.risk: low -- garbage-tolerant consumer, verified by reading the connector's config loader

allowed.reason: MEASURED 2026-09-28 (task #778): started dist/index.mjs with all four set to their literal unexpanded '${...}' strings. Before the fix it did not crash but answered initialize with protocolVersion '${MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION}', a version no client knows. Fixed in 0.1.2: an empty or unexpanded value is read as unset, the handshake returns a real version (the client's when supported), and an unconfigured tool call answers 'Slate is not configured'. Garbage-tolerant, verified by running it.
allowed.risk: LOW -- measured tolerant after the 0.1.2 fix
